title: European Commission confirms AI-generated cyberattack that took HR and other applications offline
date_note: Date of the report; Politico, relayed by Izvestia, says the attack had been going on for more than 10 days.
summary: Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier confirmed an AI-generated cyber campaign, detected 22 October, that took several applications offline. Euronews reports the attack is still ongoing and that the Commission confirmed a leak of names and email addresses from its EU Academy platform and warned of possible phishing. Citing two sources with knowledge of the matter, Euronews says the Commission suspects a China-backed network.
plain: The European Commission confirmed an AI-generated cyber campaign that took several of its applications offline. Euronews reports it is still ongoing and that names and email addresses leaked from the EU Academy platform.
exec: Euronews reports an ongoing AI-generated campaign against the Commission and a confirmed leak of EU Academy users' names and email addresses.
action: Per Euronews, the Commission is warning of possible phishing based on the leaked EU Academy names and email addresses.
impact: Several applications taken down as a protective measure, most since restored (Regnier); Sysper and MyPMO reported offline, restored early in the week of 16 Nov (heise); most staff received salaries as usual but some could not file time sheets or arrange leave (Politico, via Izvestia, citing two officials); no evidence of a data breach affecting staff as a whole detected, investigation ongoing (Regnier); per SecurityWeek, Regnier said he was not aware of a ransom demand and did not attribute the attack to a known group; per Politico, CERT-EU linked the tool ARTEX; Gazeta.ru, citing Reuters, reports Regnier said on 23 November the EU Academy platform was hit by the attack, leading to a leak of its users' personal data, with the investigation ongoing. Euronews (23 Nov) reports the attack has hit Commission systems for a month and is still ongoing, that the EU Academy website was taken offline on Saturday 21 November (Gazeta.ru, citing Reuters, gives 23 November), that the Commission confirmed a leak of names and email addresses from the EU Academy, and, citing two sources with knowledge of the matter, that the Commission suspects a China-backed network, codenamed 'Panda' internally; Euronews says the suspicion rests on the attack's sophistication and the use of ARTEX.

sources.name: The Telegraph via Yahoo News (relaying Politico)
Help Net Security (relaying the Commission briefing and Politico)

validation.note: Euronews (own anonymous official; Sysper and JSIS named) and Politico (relayed by Izvestia, Telegraph, Anadolu, La Libre) report independently; the Commission has not confirmed the scope. Politico original not read. 20 Nov: Security Affairs (19 Nov) reports CERT-EU named ARTEX as a possible tool and more than ten days of disruption; CERT-EU and Politico originals not read. 20 Nov: Help Net Security reports spokesperson Regnier confirming an AI-generated campaign at the Commission midday briefing; ARTEX link is Politico, not Commission; originals not read. 23 Nov: Gazeta.ru (23 Nov) relays Reuters quoting Regnier that the EU Academy platform was affected and users' personal data leaked; only Gazeta.ru read, Reuters original not read, academy.europa.eu answered 403, no second publisher found yet. 23 Nov (researcher 1): Euronews exclusive read (English and Russian editions): attack still ongoing, the Commission confirmed EU Academy names and email addresses leaked (a second publisher for the leak), China-backed network suspected according to two anonymous sources; no government or investigating-firm attribution read, so actor stays empty. 23 Nov (researcher 4): Ajel reports Regnier confirmed the EU Academy data leak and that users were notified on its site; Yle (citing Reuters) reports the learning platform was taken offline and most applications restored; both relay Reuters, no new independent fact.

review.note: Compared with Help Net Security, SecurityWeek, Izvestia: Regnier AI-generated quote, 22 Oct detection, no breach evidence for staff as a whole, no ransom, no attribution match.
